newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies mostly up, yen gains after comments.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies mostly up, yen gains after comments.

text.p: IMM currency futures were slightly higher early, with yen up after more comments from Japanese officials overnight.

On the heels of similar comments Sunday night, more Japanese officials were said to have voiced concern about recent moves in foreign exchange markets. Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitzuzuka told a news conference overnight that an excessively weak or strong yen is not favorable for Japan's economy.
Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso and Trade Minister Shinji Sata made similar remarks.
On Sunday night, Japanese vice finance minister Tadashi Ogawa said Japan would act appropriately to deal with "excessive" movements in the currency markets.
March yen climbed to a 1-1/2 week high overnight, buoyed by this second day of yen-bullish comments, and remained strong early Tuesday.
Still, many traders were wary of getting long March yen as worries of underlying dollar bullishness lingered.
"Fundamentals put the dollar/yen at 120.00," one IMM currency analyst said. "When they talk about not letting the yen go crazy, they're looking at a 120.00 horizon line."
"There won't be any intervening before there," he said.
Traders also said steep declines overnight in the Nikkei 225 underscored the weakness of Japan's economy.
"The Nikkei fell 550 points on worries in the economy," the floor analyst said. "I don't see how long comments can buffet that."
Several traders and analysts said IMM currency buyers should be wary.
"I'm getting short term buy signals in the currencies but it's a real mess," another trader said.
"The dollar just keeps coming back and it's really tough to be short the dollar," he said.
Technicians put yen support at $0.8700, $0.8720 and $0.008733.
Sterling eked out small gains in early IMM trade and players said the mood in the pound pit was non-commital.

Traders said they saw little impact from British Prime Minister John Major's comments about the pound earlier Tuesday. He said sterling strength was good for inflation, but said he could become concerned if the pound's rally goes to far. He said he did not think that was the position yet.
Traders pegged March sterling resistance at $1.6940 and $1.7000.

March Canadian dollar rose to the highest price since mid-December, encouraged by technical strength and followthrough from Monday's gains. Traders said Asian and European investors were heavy cash buyers of Canada's dollar.

At 0836 CST/1436 GMT, March yen rose $0.000034 to $0.008765, March marks were up $0.0013 to $0.6438, Swiss francs rose $0.0029 to $0.7469, sterling rose $0.0018 to $1.6928, Canadian dollar rose $0.0031 to $0.7388, Australian dollar rose $0.0001 to $0.7882, and Mexican peso rose $0.000300 to $0.122925.
